CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up for bilateral reduction mammoplasty

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female presenting for follow-up post bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. She reports her breasts are doing well. At a previous visit with PA Ruth Sanchez in March, a lump was noted under the left breast, but patient has not felt it since that time and attributes this to performing massages. Patient reports some concern about scar appearance, noting that one scar has widened slightly and is bothering her cosmetically. She has been using scar gel daily. Denies back pain. Reports feeling well otherwise and enjoying summertime.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Denies current lumps, hard spots, or bumps. No signs of infection or drainage.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10-10-2020)

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Family in good health

SOCIAL HISTORY
Married/lives with family. Enjoys outdoor activities.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breasts examined. Both incisions well-healed with no signs of infection, redness, or drainage. One scar noted to have widened slightly, particularly in a high-tension area. No lumps, hard spots, or bumps appreciated on palpation.

RESULTS
Clinical photographs obtained for documentation and comparison.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with excellent healing
2. Widened scar in left breast incision likely due to high tension - counseled that definitive correction would require surgical revision (excision and re-closure), but advised to defer any revision until at least one year post-operatively
3. Continue Mederma scar gel application twice daily to affected area for scar lightening and appearance
4. Continue scar massage
5. Follow-up appointment in 6 months to reassess scars and determine if revision is desired
6. Patient agrees with plan
